analysis:
The PR makes a single one-line documentation addition to docs/provider/cli-reference.md, at head line 1274. It states that App Attest serving authorization can remain visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice requires a matching fresh coordinator decision, and that both doctor summaries follow the same rule. It links to ../reference/provider-authorization.md. The supplied base units (lines 1-794) do not contain the changed area, so I could only check the surrounding context, not the patched line itself. The patch excerpt is complete and shows one added line.

The change alters no code, configuration, defaults, keys, protocol messages, or trust boundaries. It is consistent with the threat-model entries covering App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-053, T-057) and the documented requirement that the coordinator, not the provider, owns policy. Requiring a fresh decision before MDM removal advice errs toward caution, so it creates no new attack surface and weakens no mitigation.

The doctor summary behavior itself is not in the supplied evidence. The code that implements it (DoctorCommand and the related summaries) and the target page ../reference/provider-authorization.md were not supplied. I therefore cannot confirm that the doc matches the code. A mismatch would be a documentation-accuracy problem, not a security regression I can demonstrate. No findings were identified.
